title: The 5 Brightest Stars in the Night Sky, Ranked (Number 2 Is Far Away)

scenes.text: The five brightest stars at night, ranked. Number two is thirty-six times farther than number one.
Number five: Vega, in the constellation Lyra. Twenty-five light-years away, so the light you see left it twenty-five years ago.
scenes.label: Vega · mag 0.03

scenes.text: Number four: Arcturus. About thirty-seven light-years away, and the brightest star in the constellation Bootes.
scenes.label: Arcturus · mag -0.05

scenes.text: Number three: Alpha Centauri, the closest star system to the Sun. Two stars shining together as one.
scenes.label: Alpha Centauri · mag -0.27

scenes.text: Number two: Canopus. About three hundred ten light-years away, visible mainly from the Southern Hemisphere.
scenes.label: Canopus · mag -0.74

scenes.text: Number one: Sirius. Only eight point six light-years away, and almost twice as bright as Canopus.
scenes.label: Sirius · mag -1.46

description:
The five brightest stars in the night sky, ranked by how bright they look from Earth.
Number two is 36 times farther away than number one, yet it still shines almost as brightly.
Which star have you actually spotted?
first_comment: Which star have you seen? And what should we rank next?
